engineCallbackWrites.reason: The engine needs the steered items to build the request it is about to send, so it must have them synchronously. It asks only at a request boundary (turn-model.ts #prepare/#auxiliary), after every durable event the turn has published has been accepted (each publish is awaited; only transient tool_progress is not), so the queue and background-notice facts land after the turn's earlier facts and before the request that carries the items. Could go if steering became an emit-and-await event like interaction_required (#199).

The engine needs the stop/continue decision and the reminder text before it can end or continue the turn. It is called once the final response's events are accepted (turn.ts), and the goal, reminder and verification facts it writes are the decision's own receipt, so they land at the turn's stop point. Could go if normal stop became an emit-and-await decision event like interaction_required (#199).

Binds the session-owned tools for the request (goal_check, propose_goal, session_rollover, memory tools); it writes nothing itself. Those tools write their own facts (goal, rollover_requested, memory) when the engine executes them, and execution starts only after the call's tool_start_requested event is accepted (turn-tools.ts #invoke), so the writes land between that call's tool_started and tool_finished facts. Could go if those tools returned their facts in the tool result for the reader to append.

Session owns a child run: it writes branch_started, task facts and their background_notice_enqueued notices, and reads the child handle through the branch reader (session/branches.ts), which appends each child event (including top-level request_cost_recorded facts) before accepting it, the same contract as the root reader. Branch and task facts are keyed by branch and task (replay-background.ts), notices reach the parent only at a steering boundary, and the parent tool result that reports the child is still a parent event.

Consolidates the former askOrchestrator, subagents and shellTasks callbacks into Term2's app context factory. Creating the context itself does not write; the returned methods must synchronously return task controls and route questions to Session's task registry. The gate follows their closures into task_question_opened, task stop/answer facts, and background_notice_enqueued. Task facts fold per task in replay-background.ts; notices reach the parent model only at its next steering boundary; the calling tool's result still follows as an accepted turn event. Keep this deviation while these app-owned task controls write synchronously; retire it if task operations gain an explicit accepted-event protocol.
